LanguageData.tab.settings.desc: Enable and disable optional settings which effect which information is displayed
LanguageData.tab.gui.desc: Methods which are run on gui
LanguageData.tab.modder.desc: Methods which have been added by modders via Analyzer.xml
LanguageData.settings.disable.cleanup.desc: Do NOT do this if you do not know what you are doing. This will prevent analyzer from cleaning up from after itself automatically. Analyzer can be forced to manually cleanup immediately by right clicking the menu tab button and selecting 'Cleanup'
LanguageData.settings.show.icon: Show the main tab icon on the bottom bar
LanguageData.settings.long.form.names: Show methods in analyzer using long-form names (includes params)
LanguageData.settings.disable.threading: Disable multi-threaded patching, may prevent issues with assembly patching.
LanguageData.devoptions.heading: Profile
LanguageData.top.pause.analyzer: Pause/Unpause profiling that the analyzer is done, this is not equivalent to unpatching
LanguageData.top.search: Search by name or time to filter which entries show
LanguageData.top.gc.tip: This will show a rough estimate of the memory consumed and thrown away at a given time
LanguageData.top.fps.tip: This will show your calculated frames per second
LanguageData.top.tps.tip: This will show your ticks per second, ticks are the metric the game uses to quantiy time passing, multiple ticks can happen per second, the game aims to reach 60tps at 1x
LanguageData.logs.name: Name
LanguageData.logs.max.desc: The most time the method took in a single tick or frame, in milliseconds, within the samples shown at the top.
LanguageData.logs.av.desc: Average time per tick or frame, in milliseconds, over the samples shown at the top. Includes the profiled methods it calls.
LanguageData.logs.percent.desc: The method's share of the root shown at the top, averaged over the same samples. Includes the profiled methods it calls. The bar under each row shows its own time solid and the rest faded, in the same colour as the bar at the top.
LanguageData.logs.avpc.desc: Average time of a single call, in microseconds (us).
LanguageData.logs.calls.desc: Total number of calls over the samples shown at the top.
LanguageData.logs.name.desc: The profiled method. A small square before the name is a spike flag; hover the name to see what it means.
LanguageData.logs.total.desc: Total time over all the samples shown at the top, in milliseconds.
LanguageData.panel.mod.name: Mod Name
LanguageData.panel.opendnspy: Open in Dnspy (requires the local path to be set)
LanguageData.entry.gui.colonistbar.tooltip: The colonist bar along the top of the screen
LanguageData.entry.gui.dotabs.tooltip: The inspect pane which opens up upon selecting a thing
LanguageData.entry.gui.gamecomponent.tooltip: The GUI methods for each gamecomponent
LanguageData.entry.gui.resourcereadout.tooltip: The UI function for the resource readout on the left of the screen
LanguageData.entry.gui.uiroot.tooltip: A variety of OnGUI methods for various types, including; UIRoot_Play, WindowStack, AlertsReadout, MainButtonsRoot
LanguageData.entry.gui.windowstack.tooltip: The OnGUI method for the window stack, should show profiling for all active windows
LanguageData.entry.tick.jobdriver.tooltip: A breakdown of what is occuring in each job as it is being executed by a pawn
LanguageData.entry.tick.single.tooltip: A variety of tick methods, including; World, History, FilthMonitor, Storyteller
LanguageData.entry.tick.thingcomp.tooltip: Thing comps, these can be added to any ThingWithComp, this collects them all into one category
LanguageData.entry.tick.pathfinder.tooltip: Shows a variety of methods which are used in pathfinding
LanguageData.entry.tick.gamecomponent.tooltip: The Tick methods for each gamecomponent
LanguageData.entry.tick.lord.tooltip: Lords are used for group AI, like weddings, raids, traders etc
LanguageData.entry.tick.stats.tooltip: A variety of methods which are used to calculate and looking up stat-based values
LanguageData.entry.tick.mapcomponent.tooltip: The Tick method for Map Components
LanguageData.entry.tick.needs.tooltip: Shows a variety of methods which are used in Needs calculations
LanguageData.entry.tick.pawngen.tooltip: Shows methods around PawnGen and generation of pawns for raids
LanguageData.entry.tick.pawn.tooltip: The variety of methods which are called on Pawn:Tick, including a variety of trackers
LanguageData.entry.tick.room.tooltip: The method which is responsible for the updating of room stats
LanguageData.entry.tick.storyteller.tooltip: A variety of methods relating to both incident and quest generation
LanguageData.entry.tick.thinknodes.tooltip: ThinkNodes are basically sets of general job givers filtered in an ai tree, like satisfying needs, optimizing apparel, fleeing, work is all combined in a single JobGiver_Work which can be individually profiled by looking at the Work Giver profiler tab
LanguageData.entry.tick.things.tooltip: Profiles the ticking methods of various things on the map
LanguageData.entry.tick.jobgiver.tooltip: All jobs which are manually looked for in the pawns thinktree, this includes work like satisfying needs, fleeing from danger, improving worn apparel etc
LanguageData.entry.tick.workgiver.tooltip: Work Giver is only jobs done for work, that means all the jobs listed in the Work tab, this does not include jobs run by the ai for things like satisfying needs or optimizing apparel, those can be found in the ThinkNodes profile tab
LanguageData.entry.tick.world.tooltip: Tick methods for various world entries, such as; WorldPawns, Factions, Caravans
LanguageData.entry.update.alert.tooltip: The recalculate and draw methods for Alerts
LanguageData.entry.update.dynamicdraw.tooltip: The draw method for things which are drawn via the DynamicDrawManager
LanguageData.entry.update.gamecomponent.tooltip: The Update method for each gamecomponent
LanguageData.entry.update.harmonypatches.tooltip: Harmony patches added by mods (Prefixes and Postfixes only)
LanguageData.entry.update.harmonytranspilers.tooltip: Shows a semi-accurate profiling of all Harmony Transpilers, there is a writeup in the Wiki going into detail about it
LanguageData.entry.update.infocard.tooltip: A variety of methods which relate to info panels, including stats, and gui methods
LanguageData.entry.update.mapcomponent.tooltip: The Update method for Map Components
LanguageData.entry.update.transpilermethods.tooltip: Profiles entire methods that have transpiler patches, doesn't show the impact of individual changes, only the whole method, a transpiler might change how often some code in a method runs, not just call extra methods, use to compare how a method runs before and after adding a mod that patches it
LanguageData.entry.update.sectionlayer.thingsdrawlaye: Profile how long each thing takes to print
LanguageData.entry.update.sections.tooltip: Shows the regenerate method for SectionLayers (sectionlayers are things like Snow, SunShadows, Zones)
LanguageData.entry.update.pawnrenderer.tooltip: Shows the pawnrenderer function, which is responsible for the renderering of pawns and apparel
LanguageData.entry.update.sectionlayerthings.tooltip: More in-depth profiling of Section layers, including mesh creation and the TakePrintFrom function
LanguageData.entry.update.mapdrawer.tooltip: Draw method on each map section layer
LanguageData.entry.update.shooting.tooltip: Shows a variety of methods related to combat and shooting, including verbs, turrets, projectiles etc
LanguageData.entry.update.uiroot.tooltip: A variety of update methods for GUI-related functionality, such as; AlertsReadout, Messages, Tutor
LanguageData.entry.update.thoughtworker.tooltip: Thought Workers, these drive the updates of pawns thoughts
LanguageData.entry.update.frametimes.tooltip: Shows entries which correlate to the frame times of your game (how long does each frame take to complete)
LanguageData.entry.update.custom.tooltip: Custom Profiled methods in the update category
LanguageData.entry.tick.custom.tooltip: Custom Profiled methods in the tick category
LanguageData.performance.sectionlayersnow: Improve the speed of rendering for snow
LanguageData.performance.sectionlayersnow.tooltip: Replaces a Mathf.Lerp with byte multiplication in the calculation for snow colour
LanguageData.performance.lordnotifydamage: Remove some stutters for raid AI
LanguageData.performance.lordnotifydamage.tooltip: Removes a redundant damage-notification check from the Lord toils 'LordToil_AssaultColony' and 'LordToil_AssaultColonySappers'
LanguageData.performance.killaudio.tooltip: Prevent music player bugs by destructively prefixing the 'MusicManagerPlay:MusicUpdate' function
LanguageData.performance.buildingrepair.tooltip: Removes objects that are not repairable or do not have hitpoints (which the Type 'ListerBuildingsRepairable' does not filter out)
LanguageData.performance.roof.tooltip: Caches when roofs are removed / need replacing, and preventing the jobgiver from running when no state has changed
LanguageData.performance.wallsnconduits: Optimize drawing for walls and conduits
LanguageData.performance.wallsnconduits.tooltip: Set the mesh draw type for walls and conduits to 'MapMeshOnly'
LanguageData.performance.compdeepdrill.tooltip: Skips a check for the 'correct' stone under a drill, improves performance of drills when using pawns with high mining
LanguageData.performance.tempcache.tooltip: Caches safe temperature range once per tick, reducing excess cpu load from spamming it for things like pathfinding
LanguageData.performance.zoom.tooltip: Lowers the target tps when panning to reduce stuttering
LanguageData.performance.drawlabelsfix.tooltip: Optimize the drawing of pawn and animal names in-map
LanguageData.temp.section.tooltip: Caches types in the constructor for 'Section' - this should be fixed in a future rw update
LanguageData.fix.fixmodremoval: Fix mod removal, may solve grey screen issue
LanguageData.fix.fixmodremoval.tooltip: This fixes the area manager trying to loop through null area classes from missing mods
LanguageData.fix.faction.tooltip: Removes all references to deleted factions in world objects. This will solve issues when removing factions mid-save
LanguageData.frameprofiler.button.tip: Open the game's built-in Frame Profiler. Turn on "Mirror timings to the vanilla Frame Profiler" in Settings to see Analyzer's timings in it too.
LanguageData.tab.patches.desc: Harmony patches from every mod. They can run anywhere, so each row says whether it ran in ticks, frame updates or the interface, and the percentages are of the whole frame
LanguageData.logs.spikes.desc: How many runs in the samples shown at the top were spikes: over 1 ms and over 5 times the method's usual run. Hover a row's count for the details, including methods that run on a steady interval.
LanguageData.logs.header.percenttotal: Rows shown use {0} of the root, counting each row's own time once.
LanguageData.logs.header.mstotal: Rows shown add up to {0} ms.
LanguageData.logs.header.maxtotal: Rows shown add up to {0} ms at their highest.
LanguageData.logs.header.sorted: Sorted by this column. Click again for the default order.
LanguageData.logs.header.clicktosort: Click to sort by this column.
LanguageData.logs.rowbar.tip: Solid: {0} ms of its own time ({1} of the root). Faded: {2} ms including the profiled methods it calls ({3}). Averages over {4} samples, on the same scale as the bar at the top.
LanguageData.root.frame.title: Whole frame
LanguageData.root.tick.title: Game tick (TickManager.DoSingleTick)
LanguageData.root.update.title: Frame update (Root_Play.Update)
LanguageData.root.heading: {0}: {1} ms per {2}, avg of last {3} {4}. Rows: {5} ms ({6})
LanguageData.root.heading.tip: Every number in this tab is an average over the last {0} {1} (up to 2,000), measured inside the {2} only. Calls made outside it are not counted here.\n\nThe rows below use {3} ms of it, counting each row's own time once.
LanguageData.root.segment.tip: {0}\n{1} ms per {2} of its own time, {3} of the {4}
LanguageData.root.rest.tip: The whole bar is the {0}. Each coloured part is one row's own time, not counting other rows inside it, so nested rows are only counted once. The bar under each row uses the same colour and scale. This dark part is time this list doesn't cover.
LanguageData.frame.tip.poll: PollEvents: the engine reading window, mouse and keyboard events.
LanguageData.frame.tip.update: GameUpdate: the game's update. Root_Play.Update and every game tick run in here.
LanguageData.frame.tip.capture: CaptureFrame: building the frame to draw, including the map, the world and the interface (OnGUI).
LanguageData.frame.tip.other: Other engine work: everything else the engine does each frame, such as GPU memory and render queue work.
LanguageData.frame.tip.waiting: Waiting for the next frame: the main thread is idle, held back by vsync or the frame rate cap. This is not a cost; it is the headroom left before the game would drop below that rate.
LanguageData.frame.segment.tip: {0}\n{1} ms per frame, {2} of the frame
LanguageData.frame.heading: Frame map: where the work in this tab happens inside one average frame of {0} ms ({1} fps, last {2} frames)
LanguageData.frame.heading.tip: A flame graph of one average frame, all on the same scale. The top bar is the engine's own breakdown: PollEvents, GameUpdate, CaptureFrame, other engine work, and waiting for the next frame. Under the part where this tab's root runs is the root itself, and under that the rows of this list, each by its own time. So the widths show how much of the whole frame what you are looking at really costs.
LanguageData.frame.root.tip: {0}: {1} ms per {2}{3} = {4} ms per frame, {5} of the frame. It runs inside GameUpdate.
LanguageData.frame.row.tip: {0}\n{1} ms per {2} of its own time{3} = {4} ms per frame.\n{5} of the {6}, {7} of the whole frame.
LanguageData.frame.tab.heading: This tab: {0}, {1} ms per {2}, avg of last {3} {4}. Rows: {5} ms ({6})
LanguageData.frame.tab.heading.tip: Every number in this tab is an average over the last {0} {1} (up to 2,000), measured inside the {2} only. Calls made outside it are not counted here.\n\nThe rows below use {3} ms of it, counting each row's own time once. The bar under each row uses the same colour as its part of the flame graph above.
LanguageData.spike.one: 1 spike in the last {0} {1}: worst {2} ms, usual run {3} ms.
LanguageData.spike.many: {0} spikes in the last {1} {2}: worst {3} ms, usual run {4} ms.
LanguageData.spike.notinterval: These are well above its usual run, so the interval doesn't explain them.
LanguageData.spike.heavy: Each run takes about {0} ms. That's normal for this method, but it causes a regular hitch.
LanguageData.spike.light: Each run takes about {0} ms, so its time comes in bursts. That's expected.
LanguageData.stack.trace.tip: Record which code paths call this method, sample by sample, so you can click a point below and see who made the calls in it. Ticking it again starts a fresh recording.
LanguageData.stack.status.tracing: Tracing {0}: {1} stacks captured, {2} different paths. Pause the analyzer to hold the samples still.
LanguageData.stack.splitter.tip: Drag to resize the samples and the stacks below them.
LanguageData.stack.samples.hint: Click a sample to see its stacks, scroll to zoom at the mouse, drag to pan
LanguageData.stack.samples.selected: Selected: {0} ago (click it again to show all)
LanguageData.stack.sample.none: No stacks recorded for this sample.
LanguageData.stack.sample.click: Click to see who made these calls.
LanguageData.stack.title.sampled: split by caller from sampled stacks
LanguageData.stack.title.none: No stacks were recorded for the selected sample
LanguageData.stack.table.tip: Each row is one distinct call path into this method. Every call is counted. When a sample has many calls, stacks are captured for the first 128 and then for every 2nd, 4th, 8th... call, and each captured stack counts for the calls it stands for, so the split between callers is then an estimate that adds up to the real total. When the row you selected is one type of a shared method (such as Pawn under Tick Things), only calls on that type are recorded. Called from is the method that made the call. Patches counts the Harmony patches on every method along the path. Click a row to see its full call stack.
LanguageData.stack.select: Select a row to see its full call stack
LanguageData.stack.full: Full call stack, nearest caller first. Click a method to profile it
